title: Iran's leader warns war will widen if US strikes again; Guards claim four tankers hit mines
dek: A day after the US midterms, Mojtaba Khamenei says no one should expect Washington to change course, Iran's Revolutionary Guards say four tankers are burning south of Hormuz, and Trump says he would 'do it again'.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned on Wednesday that the war with the United States would become "much wider" if American attacks were repeated, and said anyone expecting Washington's policy to change after Tuesday's midterm elections was "seriously mistaken". The written statement, published on his website, came hours after Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said four oil tankers had been destroyed by naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz.

In Washington, President Donald Trump acknowledged that the Iran war was "part" of the reason his Republican party lost both houses of Congress, but said in an interview: "I did the right thing. I would have done it again." Mediators from Qatar, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are still passing proposals between the two sides, and none of the claims about the tankers has been independently confirmed.

## What happened

The IRGC said on Wednesday morning that four oil tankers it described as non-compliant had struck naval mines while using a route south of the strait that Iran has "prohibited for navigation", and that they "are still burning". It said two other vessels had been halted, and that its air defences had shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the strait at 4.30 am local time, which it called the 56th such drone it had downed. The Guards gave no names, flags or crew details for any of the ships, and no shipping authority or owner had confirmed the losses by Wednesday evening. US Central Command has previously said the main shipping lanes through the strait have been cleared of mines.

The IRGC claim followed an attack on Tuesday that the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) did confirm: a tanker was hit in its engine room by two unidentified projectiles about 14 nautical miles north-east of Limah, on Oman's Musandam peninsula. No casualties were reported in that incident, and no one claimed it. One news agency said it could not establish whether the two incidents were linked.

Khamenei's statement was aimed at those who hoped the midterm results would soften US policy. "Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change" through partisan shifts or through concessions are "seriously mistaken", it said, according to translations carried in reports. "Should such aggressions be repeated, the war's scope will become much wider," it said. Khamenei, who succeeded his father after Ali Khamenei was killed in US-Israeli strikes earlier this year, has not been seen or heard in public since; US officials believe he was seriously wounded, reports said, and he has communicated only through written messages.

Iran's chief negotiator, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, took a different line on the election itself. "Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," he wrote on X, adding that if Washington ignored its voters "it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare".

## What Washington says

Trump confirmed in an interview that US forces had struck an anti-aircraft site on Iran's Qeshm Island early on Tuesday, calling it a "minor attack" that "wasn't war". US officials have described the strikes as defensive, saying they followed Iranian fire at an American aircraft over the strait.

Asked in the interview about the midterm losses, Trump said "part of it was Iran", and that "people understand the importance of what I've done". In another interview on Tuesday evening he said he had no immediate plan for new strikes: "We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it." He also said, "We seem to be getting everything we want." One report said that Trump has leaned towards a large attack but has not decided, according to a summary of it in another report. Another report said earlier that Central Command was ready to begin a short campaign as early as Wednesday.

## Background

The war began on 28 February with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil passed before the war, and says it will reopen it within two days only if the US meets seven conditions, including the lifting of oil sanctions, an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and the release of frozen funds. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Tuesday that the latest US reply was "not convincing".

A Qatari official told reporters that mediators had put forward "a new suggestion to move the process along" and expected feedback from both sides within 36 hours. Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, said both sides "remain committed to the negotiation process".

The conflict has spread across the region. Yemen's Houthis, who are aligned with Iran, said on Wednesday that they had hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile, causing "extensive damage", and urged airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. They also claimed missile strikes on Saudi forces in al-Jawf. Saudi authorities had not commented, and the claims are unverified. Houthi strikes on Saudi airports in October killed at least 20 people, mostly at the Riyadh airport, reports said.

## China's position

China's foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said on Wednesday that "the pressing priority is to avoid resumption of conflicts in the Middle East". She said China would "support Iran and the U.S. in resolving disputes through negotiations" and help "seek a proper and comprehensive settlement on the opening of the Strait of Hormuz", after Foreign Minister Wang Yi met Saudi and Iranian national security officials separately in Beijing. China is the largest buyer of Iranian crude oil.

## Why it matters for India

India imports most of its crude oil, and a large share of its oil and gas has historically come through Hormuz. Brent crude settled at $103.60 a barrel on Tuesday, its lowest close since 7 October, reports said, but prices remain far above pre-war levels. Any new round of strikes, or confirmed losses of tankers, would push up the cost of fuel, fertiliser and shipping for India.

The danger to Indian crews is direct. An Indian seafarer was killed on Monday when the Indian-flagged vessel MSV Al Jusufi was attacked off Oman, and the external affairs ministry condemned the attack. Millions of Indians live and work in the Gulf, including in Saudi Arabia, where the Houthis say they have struck the capital's main airport.

## What happens next

- Qatari mediators expect replies from Washington and Tehran on their latest proposal within about 36 hours of Tuesday's talks.
- Trump says no decision has been taken on new strikes; US reports say plans are ready.
- China's Middle East envoy is due to visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia later in November.
- Shipping authorities have yet to confirm the IRGC's claim about the four tankers.
